note: src/facts.rs lines 18-175: `ExtentEntry` has fields key, label, world_root, world_state, kind, pattern, out_len, matcher. FOUR of them already carry `#[serde(default)]` with an explicit "absence means not-recorded" reading: world_root ("`world_root` is `#[serde(default)]` for entries minted before it existed"), kind ("`None` means *not recorded*, never *some default kind*"), out_len ("`None` means *not recorded*, never *zero*"), and matcher ("`None` means *not recorded*, never *some default grammar*"). `pattern` is `#[serde(default)]` too but defaults to empty string rather than an Option. The census predicate `ExtentEntry::censuses` requires, among other conjuncts, `self.key == self.world_root` — it compares the KEY (not the label) against the world root, and its doc says "Both halves of the comparison are tool-captured: the key by `observe::search_key`, the root by `worldstate`."

src/facts.rs lines 505-575, `pub fn mint`: the fold from the pending buffer into a fact's extent is a pure field-by-field copy — `key: e.key.clone(), label: e.label.clone()` — so `mint` never computes or rewrites a label; whatever the pending entry carries is what the fact stores, and key and label are independent fields. The pin is computed over, per pending entry in order, `e.label`, `e.world_root`, `e.world_state`, `e.output`, each followed by a newline, then sha256. The pin therefore hashes the LABEL and does NOT hash the key. The comment says the pin is "a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker".

src/observe.rs. `resolve_key` (lines 35-37) sets the key to `fs::canonicalize(path)` when that succeeds and the path as given otherwise — so the key is canonical-absolute by construction. `search_key` (lines 56-67) resolves a search root and, when it canonicalizes to the same directory as `world_root`, stores world_root's own spelling instead, "so it is about *which directory*, never about how either tool wrote it down". In the plain `look` path (lines ~368-405) the LABEL is a different value from the key: with no line range it is `path.to_string()` — the path exactly as the caller spelled it — and with a range it is `format!("{path} lines {a}-{end}")`. The pending entry's `output` is `shown` (the file contents or the selected range) and does not include the `==> {path} <==` header, which goes only into `printed`. `world.root` is already computed at this point, from the observed path (`worldstate::Session::new().for_path(p)`), and is stored on the same pending entry.

Repo-wide sweep for the word `pin` across all .rs files in src/ and tests/ (two greps), plus the two sites that matter. Findings: (a) `sha256_hex(&hash_input)` at src/facts.rs:556 is the only place a fact pin is computed — no other site recomputes one, and no site compares two fact pins for equality outside tests; (b) the only tests asserting anything about fact pins are tests/authoring_cli.rs `two_facts_from_identical_observations_pin_identically` and `a_fact_taken_against_a_changed_tree_pins_differently` (lines 3221-3302), which assert only that two pins minted in the same run are equal / unequal and hard-code no pin literal, and which drive the CLI with a RELATIVE path (`look f.txt`, cwd = the test repo); (c) src/evidence.rs:399 copies `fact.pin` into a recorded evidence statement (`pin: Some(fact.pin.clone())`) without recomputing it; (d) src/query.rs:13 prints it. Every disjunct is decidable from the memo, its evidence file and its snapshot, and each of the first four reuses a set the crate already computes.", 6932: "The third disjunct of the decided predicate is not well defined, on two counts, and the claim's closing sentence (\"each of the first four reuses a set the crate already computes\") does not hold for it. (a) \"The pin stored on its records\" is written as a single value; it is not. Replay of tet30's ledger: 125 records, 61 distinct pin values in that one file, and all 13 claims carry records with more than one distinct pin \u2014 C11 has 16, C10 and C12 have 8 each. The predicate does not say whether rule 3 fires when any, all, or the latest of a claim's record pins differs, and the three answers give different owed sets. (b) The comparison is between a per-fact `sha256:` content fingerprint (src/facts.rs 405-452) and a prose-parsed git token (src/ledger.rs 150-205), so no crate set is being reused here \u2014 unlike disjuncts 1, 2 and 4, this one is a new predicate over records, and it is the only disjunct with no existing computation behind it. Disjuncts 1, 2, 4 and 5 are unaffected by this record." 6936: "Four of the five disjuncts hold as stated and the closing summary is right for them. A \"discovery\" is defined in this replay as a cross-workspace regrade giving a verdict no EARLIER workspace gave, so its ordinal is at least 2 for any ledger that could ever be replayed; the observed ordinals are [2,2,2,2,2,3,4]. Capping at one workspace per wording therefore retains zero discoveries by identity, on this ledger and on every other, including one where a floor would be worthless. So \"a rule with no confirmation floor would have retained none of the seven\" does not measure the floor's necessity \u2014 it restates the definition. Likewise N=4 retaining all seven is fixed by the maximum observed ordinal being 4. The empirical content of the replay is the ordinal distribution and the cost curve, and that content supports the weaker and still-useful proposition the memo could have made: five of the seven arrive at the second workspace, so N=2 buys 5/7 for 16 extra gradings. The sentence \"the floor is therefore what carries the discovery property\" is the one that spends the definitional figure as though it were an observation. Context worth stating: only 16 of the 35 pairs were ever graded by two or more distinct workspaces at all." 13643: "Every figure reproduces on an independent replay of tet30's ledger: 35 (claim, digest) pairs, 69 unbounded workspace-gradings, 7 discoveries at ordinals 5/1/1, the curve 35/51/60/67 at N=1..4, and N=2 buying five of the seven for sixteen gradings above the dirty-only floor. The final clause does not hold. \"Each further N buys less\" is false at the step this design's default turns on: N=2->N=3 costs 9 gradings for 1 discovery, N=3->N=4 costs 7 gradings for the last 1. The marginal price per discovery falls from nine to seven, so returns are not monotonically diminishing in cost, and the run also shows N=4 retaining all seven discoveries at 67 of the 69 gradings full re-grading performs \u2014 a cap at 4 forgoes nothing and saves two. The prose at memo line 11, \"every further step buys less for more\", carries the same error. "Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.

The acknowledgement event cannot live in `prose.jsonl`. `ProseEvent` is an internally-tagged serde enum over exactly `Create` and `Revise`, and `workspace::read_jsonl` propagates any line's parse failure as an error over the whole log rather than skipping it; empirically, a build at this pin reading a `prose.jsonl` containing one valid `Create` line and one `{"event":"Ack",...}` line fails the entire read with `unknown variant \`Ack\`, expected \`Create\` or \`Revise\`` and exits 1. A new tag value therefore makes every older build unable to read even the prose it already understood.

The rendered section follows compose.rs's shipped conventions with one deliberate difference. A "## Transplants" section renders beside the modification-target section: per live transplant, the donor fact id with its extent labels (labels, never absolute keys — the committed-document rule), the destination target id and symbol, and one entry per live premise carrying the selected text verbatim in a fenced block with the discharging claim id beside it; withdrawn transplants and premises are dropped, and once any claim exists the section renders even when empty ("none declared"), because the hole is the finding — the same visibility answer to under-declaration the target section shipped. The deliberate difference: compose.rs refuses to inline captured output into the document because output is unbounded, but a premise is an author-bounded selection, not a whole capture, so inlining it verbatim is both safe and the entire point — the reader must see the donor's clause on the page, spelled the way the donor's file spells it, or the section is a list of opaque pointers. Fenced blocks rather than table cells because a premise legitimately spans lines and markdown table cells cannot carry multi-line verbatim text without escaping, which would violate byte-fidelity.

435:   "text": "The two code sites the exclusion mechanism has to fit between.

(1) src/facts.rs lines 82-103, `ExtentEntry::censuses` — TET-28's census predicate in full. It reads exactly five things: that `kind` is Some(Search) or Some(NoMatch), that `pattern` byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `worldstate::NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root`. It never reads `label` and never reads `output`. Its doc comment states the predicate "is about existence and rooting, never about what was found".

(2) src/observe.rs lines 158-195, the head of `look_grep`. It refuses a non-existent root, then builds the argument vector: `-r` ONLY when `root_path.is_dir()`, then `-I`, `-n`, `-H`, `-e`, the pattern, and finally `root` — passed through verbatim as the caller spelled it, never canonicalized. `Command::new("grep")` is then invoked with that vector and the whole stdout is taken with `String::from_utf8_lossy`.",

7647:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: "a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a "showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes — the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests "what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches "would not pin identically".

The second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries "are built separately... neither reads the other" — today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value ("a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone — which is the design's own defect back again.

What survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

710:   "prop": "A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry — the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing " in " or "(grep: " would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry — the observation kind and the search pattern — following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as "predates the field, not eligible" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.",

3112:   "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with "\n", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored — so "substring of fact.output" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then "verbatim substring of a single observation's output", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts — re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.",
3116:     "Verified in facts.rs at the pinned commit: mint builds output by joining non-empty entry outputs with "\n" (filter !e.output.is_empty(), matching the claim's "skipping zero-length entries" reconstruction rule); ExtentEntry stores no per-entry output length or boundary, so the seam-straddling unsoundness is real; and kind/pattern are both #[serde(default)] fields added for TET-28 with the documented "None means not recorded, never some default kind" reading and the re-run remedy — exactly the schema precedent the fix mirrors."
3120:     "The unsoundness is real and stated by the mint path: mint() builds output by filtering out empty entry outputs and joining the rest with "\n", and ExtentEntry stores key/label/world_root/world_state/kind/pattern only — no per-entry length, so entry boundaries inside Fact.output are unrecoverable and a substring can straddle the seam. The proposed fix mirrors the shipped precedent exactly: kind and pattern are both #[serde(default)] fields added for TET-28, with "None means *not recorded*, never *some default kind*", and targets.rs already treats pre-field facts as ineligible with re-grep as the remedy. The skip-zero-length reconstruction matches the mint-time !e.output.is_empty() filter."
3150:   "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with "\n", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored — so "substring of fact.output" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then "verbatim substring of a single observation's output", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts — re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.",

9237:   "prop": "TET-28's census predicate needs no change, and this is what makes the two disclosures divide cleanly. `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads exactly five things — that the kind is `Search` or `NoMatch`, that the pattern byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root` — and never reads `label` or `output`. A worktree-rooted search therefore still censuses after this change, correctly, because the predicate was always about a search's existence and rooting rather than about what it found. What changes is not the predicate but what a passing census entitles a reader to conclude, and that is carried by text: a standing line in `check` saying the exclusion policy exists, and the search record's own `label` saying which patterns this particular search was given.",

14556:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: "a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a "showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes — the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests "what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches "would not pin identically".

The second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries "are built separately... neither reads the other" — today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value ("a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone — which is the design's own defect back again.

What survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

The Facts table (src/compose.rs:280-305) emits `| ID | Note | Extent (captured) | Rests under |` and fills Extent with each extent entry's label joined by "; " — no captured output and no key is rendered anywhere in that loop, so a reader holding the document has nothing to recompute from. 441:   "text": "The census predicate does not need to know, and should not be taught to. `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads five things — the record's kind, its pattern, that its world root is a real git root, and that the search key equals that root — and reads neither the label nor the output. It was always a predicate about a search's existence and where it started rather than about what the search saw, which is why a symbol with no occurrences is censused by the grep establishing it has none. That property is what lets this change through untouched: a worktree-rooted search is still a worktree-rooted search after it stops walking into snapshot directories. What moves is not the predicate but what a reader may conclude from one, and that is a matter of text in two places — a standing line in `check` saying the policy exists, and the search record's own label saying which exclusions this search was actually given.",
1256:   "text": "TET-28's refusal is untouched, and its wording needs no amendment. It fires on `ExtentEntry::censuses`, which reads the search's existence and its root out of an extent that is immutable once minted and that a bound on `printed` never reaches. More to the point, the refusal already tells the truth about its own scope: it "is about the search's existence and where it was rooted, never about what it found". A design that bounds what the author is shown does not make that sentence any less accurate — it was never a claim about what the author read.",

5:    "prop": "A census check cannot be built on labels, and the record model already shows the right way to extend the schema. At mint time only key, label, world_root and world_state survive into an ExtentEntry — the observation's kind is dropped, and the grep pattern exists only inside a display label, where an author-chosen pattern containing " in " or "(grep: " would make parsing ambiguous. The census therefore needs the new root-level search entry to carry two structured fields into ExtentEntry — the observation kind and the search pattern — following the exact precedent world_root set: #[serde(default)], with the empty value read as "predates the field, not eligible" rather than guessed about. Legacy facts can then never satisfy a census requirement, whose remedy is precisely to re-run the grep under the new capture. The snapshot already ships facts.jsonl with full extent entries, so check reads these fields from files every snapshot already contains; and because no surface lets an author supply an extent by hand, both sides of the rooting comparison and the pattern are tool-captured by construction.",

C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a "showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes — the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests "what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches "would not pin identically".

The second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries "are built separately... neither reads the other" — today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value ("a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone — which is the design's own defect back again.

What survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

627:    "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. Fact.output is built at mint by joining the buffer entries' non-empty outputs with "\n", and the per-entry boundaries are not stored — so "substring of fact.output" can be satisfied by text straddling the seam between two observations: bytes that were never contiguous in anything the author actually saw, e.g. the tail of one file's capture concatenated with the head of another's. The fix is a serde-defaulted per-entry field on ExtentEntry recording the entry's output byte length, mirroring exactly how kind and pattern were added for TET-28: boundaries become reconstructible from lengths (skipping zero-length entries, matching the mint-time filter), the premise relation is then "verbatim substring of a single observation's output", and a donor fact minted before the field existed is ineligible with the same remedy TET-28 gives legacy facts — re-look and re-mint. Absent means not recorded, never guessed.",

643:        "note": "The unsoundness is real and stated by the mint path: mint() builds output by filtering out empty entry outputs and joining the rest with "\n", and ExtentEntry stores key/label/world_root/world_state/kind/pattern only — no per-entry length, so entry boundaries inside Fact.output are unrecoverable and a substring can straddle the seam. The proposed fix mirrors the shipped precedent exactly: kind and pattern are both #[serde(default)] fields added for TET-28, with "None means *not recorded*, never *some default kind*", and targets.rs already treats pre-field facts as ineligible with re-grep as the remedy. The skip-zero-length reconstruction matches the mint-time !e.output.is_empty() filter."

1963:    "prop": "TET-28's census predicate needs no change, and this is what makes the two disclosures divide cleanly. `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads exactly five things — that the kind is `Search` or `NoMatch`, that the pattern byte-equals the symbol, that `world_root` is non-empty and not `NO_GIT`, and that `key == world_root` — and never reads `label` or `output`. A worktree-rooted search therefore still censuses after this change, correctly, because the predicate was always about a search's existence and rooting rather than about what it found. What changes is not the predicate but what a passing census entitles a reader to conclude, and that is carried by text: a standing line in `check` saying the exclusion policy exists, and the search record's own `label` saying which patterns this particular search was given.",
3558:        "note": "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: "a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a "showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes — the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests "what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches "would not pin identically".

The second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries "are built separately... neither reads the other" — today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value ("a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone — which is the design's own defect back again.

What survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

The refusal text at targets.rs:171 already ends "The refusal is about the search's existence and where it was rooted, never about what it found", which is exactly the disclaimer a bounded return would otherwise need added."

692:    "prop": "Containment against a fact's whole output has one genuine unsoundness, and it is fixable by the same schema move TET-28 already made. 717:        "note": "The unsoundness is real and stated by the mint path: mint() builds output by filtering out empty entry outputs and joining the rest with "\n", and ExtentEntry stores key/label/world_root/world_state/kind/pattern only — no per-entry length, so entry boundaries inside Fact.output are unrecoverable and a substring can straddle the seam. Every candidate symbol here was priced first: `look_grep` costs 709,469 bytes, `NON_COVERAGE` 858,096, `censuses` 691,562, `look_path` 688,776, `search_key` 633,291. The interesting number is not any one of them but the floor they share \u2014 roughly 0.63 MB is returned whichever symbol is asked for, because it is not about the symbol at all. Dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone removes between 95.9% and 99.9% of each. So the census requirement is today priced by tetel's own accumulated output rather than by the code being censused: two thirds of a megabyte comes back from grep, and is stored in the fact, per declared target.",

(a) src/observe.rs:342-412 `look_path`: the key is `resolve_key(p)` and the world marker is `worldstate::Session::new().for_path(p)` — both derived from the observed file, so an entry's `world_root` is the repository *the observed file lives in*, not the repository the caller was working in. (b) src/observe.rs:35-42 `resolve_key` falls back infallibly to `path.display()` when `fs::canonicalize` fails, so the key is NOT absolute by construction. src/observe.rs:56-67 `search_key` returns `world_root`'s own spelling when the search root and the world root canonicalize to the same directory.

(c) src/mcp.rs:177 `fn resolved` joins a relative path onto `std::env::current_dir()` rather than refusing it; its doc comment says "Nothing here changes *which* file is opened". The `look` handler (src/mcp.rs:759) never calls `resolved`: it forwards `p.path` verbatim into `observe::LookRequest::Open { path: Some(p.path), ... }` / `Grep { root: Some(p.path) }`. The MCP `look` tool description says `path` "must be a regular file (or a symlink to one)" and nowhere requires it to be absolute. note:
Constructed and captured on the release build at target/release/tetel: the symlink-into-a-different-repository case that defeats the key-derived rule anchored to the entry's own world_root.

Fixture: `outer/` is a git repository holding `README.md` and `x.txt` (contents "OUTER x"); `otherrepo/` is a separate git repository holding `x.txt` (contents "OTHER FILE"); `outer/link` is a committed symlink to `otherrepo`. `git -C outer rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers `.../outer`; the same command run inside `outer/link` answers `.../otherrepo`.

Attack: `tetel look .../outer/link/x.txt` mints an entry with key `.../otherrepo/x.txt`, label `.../outer/link/x.txt`, world_root `.../otherrepo`. The key is strictly under that entry's own world_root, so a rule that strips world_root from the key mints the relative label `x.txt` — not a refusal and not absolute. Rendered in a memo shipping in `outer`, `x.txt` resolves to `outer/x.txt`, a file that exists and holds "OUTER x" against the observed "OTHER FILE". This is silently-wrong, and it is reached with an ordinary symlink rather than a nested or vendored checkout.

Discriminator, captured: on the same build the caller's own spelling and the entry's world_root disagree here — the label `.../outer/link/x.txt` does not begin with world_root `.../otherrepo`. In the control observation, `tetel look .../outer/README.md`, key, label and world_root all agree: key and label are both `.../outer/README.md` and world_root is `.../outer`, so the spelling does begin with world_root. So requiring the caller's spelling to lie under the same world_root the key is relativized against separates the two cases on evidence available at capture, with no new tool invoked.

src/worldstate.rs:195-204 `Session::for_path` is why: it takes the containing directory and `fs::canonicalize`s it before asking git, so a path reached through a symlink is attributed to the tree the symlink points into, never to the tree the caller navigated from.

19:The half-promise that came out of the contract deserves its own paragraph, because an earlier draft said "and is spelled absolute otherwise" and that sentence was not deliverable by anything this design builds. Nothing between a caller's argv and the stored label absolutizes a relative spelling. Constructed and captured on the release build: with the working directory in no repository at all, `look ../outer/x.txt` mints a key strictly under `outer`'s own root and a `world_root` that is that real repository — two of the three conditions — and stores the label `../outer/x.txt`. It lands in the "otherwise" branch and is relative, anchored to a working directory no reader of the memo has. Run from inside that repository, `look x.txt` stores `x.txt`, which is character-for-character what the root-relative rule would have minted. Two things follow. The caller-spelling condition has to say what a relative spelling is measured against, and the answer this design takes is a lexical join onto the process's working directory with no symlink resolution: both fixture arms then resolve under their own `world_root` and are relativized properly, while the symlink into another repository is refused exactly as before, its spelling being absolute already and outside the answering root. And the residue that still fails the condition cannot be promised absolute without a rewrite this ticket does not take on. The only absolutization on offer is a join onto the *process's* directory — what `fn resolved` does for the MCP handlers that call it, over a doc comment saying the server cannot know the caller's working directory — so keeping the promise would mean storing a path anchored to a directory the caller never chose and the memo never names, trading one unresolvable label for another. It would also rewrite labels for observations this design otherwise leaves alone, every relative-spelled `look` including the two CLI pin tests, and move their pins for a reason that has nothing to do with root-relativization. So the promise is dropped and the case is carried as a named risk instead, with the marker rather than the shape of the string as what distinguishes a root-relative label from a caller's own relative one — and, since the marker does not render, with `check` naming relative labels that carry none.

note:
Condition three's two candidate resolution rules, captured on the release build `tetel 0.1.0` at HEAD 01b140c in a fresh scratch tree `<s>` holding two real one-file git repositories `outer` (x.txt = "OUTER x", with a committed symlink `link -> ../otherrepo`) and `otherrepo` (x.txt = "OTHER FILE"), plus a sibling directory in no repository.

Three observations actually captured (pending.json read back verbatim):
- `tetel look link/x.txt` with cwd `<s>/outer`: key `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/otherrepo`, label `link/x.txt` — a RELATIVE caller spelling on an entry whose world_root is a real repository with the key strictly under it.
- `tetel look ../otherrepo/x.txt` with cwd `<s>/outer`: key `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/otherrepo`, label `../otherrepo/x.txt`.
- control `tetel look x.txt` with cwd `<s>/outer`: key `<s>/outer/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/outer`, label `x.txt`.

Truth table for "the caller's spelling lies under world_root", computed lexically over those spellings under each candidate rule (LEXICAL NORMALIZATION = collapse `..` textually; NON-NORMALIZING JOIN = concatenate cwd and the spelling, collapsing nothing):
- cwd `<s>/sibling` (no repository), spelling `../outer/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/outer`: normalizing -> `<s>/outer/x.txt`, condition HOLDS; non-normalizing -> `<s>/sibling/../outer/x.txt`, condition FAILS.
- cwd `<s>/outer`, spelling `x.txt`, world_root `<s>/outer`: normalizing -> `<s>/outer/x.txt`, HOLDS; non-normalizing -> `<s>/outer/x.txt`, HOLDS.
- cwd `<s>/outer`, spelling `../otherrepo/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/otherrepo`: normalizing -> `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, HOLDS (so all three conditions hold and a bare `x.txt` would be minted anchored to otherrepo, resolving in the shipping tree `outer` to the different file "OUTER x"); non-normalizing -> `<s>/outer/../otherrepo/x.txt`, FAILS.
- cwd `<s>/outer`, spelling `link/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/otherrepo`: FAILS under both rules.

So the normalizing rule admits both C30 fixture arms but also admits the cross-repository `..` escape; the non-normalizing join refuses the escape, refuses C30's first arm, and admits only the second arm and the `link/x.txt` case is refused either way.

1311:   "text": "Contrary to the reading that return and capture are one value in `look_path`: at src/observe.rs:314-330 `printed` is a distinct `String::new()` that receives a COPY of `shown` via `printed.push_str(&shown)` (a borrow), and only afterwards is `shown` MOVED into `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }`. 1483:   "text": "Two things that together make the zero-content case reachable and make a `look_path` shortfall recomputable from shipped bytes. (1) `look_path` (src/observe.rs:277-300) refuses exactly two conditions \u2014 a path that does not exist, and a directory \u2014 and then does `fs::read_to_string(p)` on whatever remains. No exclusion filtering is applied on this path at all: the only construction of `Exclusions` in the module is `Exclusions::decide(root_path)` at observe.rs:389, inside `look_grep`, and `decide` itself returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any root that is not a directory. So a tracked path under a `.tetel/` snapshot directory is opened by `look <path>` like any other file, and the four long-line ledgers are reachable. (2) `snapshot.rs`'s `SNAPSHOT_FILES` (src/snapshot.rs:71-100) is a ten-entry enumeration whose first element is `facts.jsonl`, so every fact's persisted `output` \u2014 for a `Path` entry, the complete selected text \u2014 ships beside the rendered memo. The enumeration's own comment says the list is enumerated rather than copied wholesale so that shipping a workspace file is a deliberate decision.",
1503:   "text": "What `look_path` selects and what it wraps that selection in, read at src/observe.rs:277-337 for the purpose of settling the budget's referent on the path side. (1) The selected text is `shown`: with no `--lines` it is `contents.clone()`, the whole file; with `--lines a:b` it is `all[a - 1..end].join(\"\\n\")` over `contents.lines()`, where `end = b.min(total)` \u2014 so the selection is 1-based, begins at line `a`, and is joined without a trailing newline. (2) `printed` is a separate `String::new()` assembled in up to three pushes: `printed.push_str(&format!(\"==> {path} <==\\n\"))`, then `printed.push_str(&shown)`, then a single `'\\n'` if `shown` is non-empty and does not already end in one. (3) The header therefore exists in `printed` and in no other place: `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the selection alone, so neither the header nor the trailing-newline pad is ever part of the captured output, the label, the key or anything that ships in the snapshot. A budget measured over the assembled `printed` would consume the header before any content, and would count `==> ` plus the path plus ` <==\\n` against the file's own bytes; a budget measured over `shown` counts only what was selected.",
1532:     "why": "This shows the fields assigned in one `look_path` entry, but the captured material does not cover the implementations of `resolve_key`, `pending::save`, or the snapshot contents, so the claims about what is ever part of anything shipping in the snapshot range beyond the evidence.",
1616:   "text": "In `look_path` the label is finished before the string the bound applies to exists \u2014 the opposite statement order from `look_grep`. `let (shown, label) = match lines { ... };` completes at observe.rs:297-312 and fixes `label` in all three of its arms (`path.to_string()`, the \"nothing in range\" form, and `{path} lines {a}-{end}`), and only afterwards, at observe.rs:314, does `let mut printed = String::new()` begin assembling the return. The label is then moved into `PendingEntry { label, .. }` at 321-330 unchanged. So an implementer who bounds `printed` at 316 where `shown` is pushed, and leaves the `match lines` block untouched, gets a cut return with a label that says nothing about the cut, which is the silent cut the design exists to stop. In `look_grep` the same edit is naturally safe: `printed.push_str(&stdout)` at observe.rs:438 opens the match branch and the `Search` label is built afterwards at 457-460.",

7647:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

7893:     "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. That state is reachable here, not hypothetical: F1(7) finds four tracked files in this worktree with a single line over 32768 bytes (up to 905745), and F1(4) confirms `look_path` filters nothing, so any of them can be opened directly. The claim as written establishes only that the cut must fall on a line boundary; it does not establish that a line-boundary cut always returns something, and the design nowhere states what happens when it returns nothing. Either state the floor (admit at least one line, cutting it mid-line and saying so) or state explicitly that a line longer than the budget is unreturnable \u2014 the current wording leaves an implementer to discover the zero-byte case in production."

7901:     "The conclusion survives; the inference stated for it does not. Measured (F1): in all four files the long line sits at position 11/15, 15, 2 and 2 \u2014 never position 1 \u2014 with first lines of 978, 882, 1273 and 1237 bytes. 8228:   "prop": "The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.",
8232:     "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. So the asymmetry is not \"a consequence of the code's shape\"; it is a choice the design is entitled to make but has not justified. This matters because C9 is an instruction to an implementer \u2014 it tells them the `look <path>` case is closed by construction, which suppresses the observation that after f3 ships, `look <path>` on a large file is still silently cut by the caller with no trace anywhere, the very defect the ticket names."

8660:     "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
8664:     "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
8672:     "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

8860:     "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

2704:   "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",

2926:   "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
2930:     "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
2938:     "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."

9411:   "prop": "No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.",
9415:     "Escape hatches 1 and 3: look_path opens any single named file with no traversal and nothing in this design touches it; run_command has only the empty-argv refusal between entry and `Command::new(&argv[0]).spawn()`, with no inspection of the command or its paths, so it offers no place to apply an exclusion."

14556:     "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

14793:     "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. That state is reachable here, not hypothetical: F1(7) finds four tracked files in this worktree with a single line over 32768 bytes (up to 905745), and F1(4) confirms `look_path` filters nothing, so any of them can be opened directly. The claim as written establishes only that the cut must fall on a line boundary; it does not establish that a line-boundary cut always returns something, and the design nowhere states what happens when it returns nothing. Either state the floor (admit at least one line, cutting it mid-line and saying so) or state explicitly that a line longer than the budget is unreturnable \u2014 the current wording leaves an implementer to discover the zero-byte case in production."
14797:     "Everything measurable here checks out: grep is run with -I -n -H so its output line is `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` and `look_grep` splits on `stdout.lines()`; exactly four tracked paths hold a single line over 32768 bytes, up to 905745, and all four are *.tetel/facts.jsonl snapshot ledgers (F3); a whole-`src` grep for `is_char_boundary`, `char_indices` and `.truncate(` returns no hits at all (F3); the longest single line carries 1922 UTF-8 continuation bytes (F6). The clause that does not hold as written is \"`look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory\": `look_path` has a third refusal in its body, `invalid --lines range {a}:{b}` when `a < 1 || a > b` (observe.rs:300-302). The conclusion the clause is used for is unaffected \u2014 no exclusion filtering is applied and a plain `look <path>` with no range reaches none of the three refusals, so each of the four ledgers is readable directly \u2014 but the enumeration is incomplete."
14801:     "The conclusion survives; the inference stated for it does not. C5 argues: the whole-lines-only rule \"admits a return of no content at all whenever the first candidate line by itself exceeds the budget, and that state is reachable on tracked files here rather than hypothetical: exactly four tracked paths in this worktree hold a single line longer than 32768 bytes \u2026 while `look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory and applies no exclusion filtering, so each is readable directly\".\n\nHolding a long line somewhere is not the same as the FIRST candidate line being over budget, and the claim's evidence establishes only the former. Measured (F1): in all four files the long line sits at position 11/15, 15, 2 and 2 \u2014 never position 1 \u2014 with first lines of 978, 882, 1273 and 1237 bytes. Reading each of them \"directly\", i.e. a plain `look <path>`, returns 5, 2, 1 and 1 whole lines (24948, 11977, 1274, 1238 bytes) and never zero content.\n\nThe condition C5 does not state, and needs: the zero-content state arises on a read whose selection BEGINS with the over-budget line \u2014 a ranged `look --lines k:\u2026` with the long line at k (`--lines 15:20` on tet46, `--lines 2:2` on tet29). 15113:     "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. 15530:     "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
15534:     "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
15542:     "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

What is conditional is only the empty-selection form `{path} lines {a}-{b} (file has {total} line(s); nothing in range)`. The analogy therefore overstates the existing convention; the proposed \"absence means whole\" behaviour for the shortfall segment is not itself in question."

15868:     "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

15979:     "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
15987:     "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
15991:     "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."
