380:   "text": "This design ran into its own subject before it could declare a single modification target, and the shape of that is worth stating rather than working around quietly. TET-28 requires a symbol an implementer is told to modify to be censused by a grep of the whole worktree. Every candidate symbol here was priced first: `look_grep` costs 709,469 bytes, `NON_COVERAGE` 858,096, `censuses` 691,562, `look_path` 688,776, `search_key` 633,291. The interesting number is not any one of them but the floor they share \u2014 roughly 0.63 MB is returned whichever symbol is asked for, because it is not about the symbol at all. Dropping snapshot directories and evidence ledgers alone removes between 95.9% and 99.9% of each. So the census requirement is today priced by tetel's own accumulated output rather than by the code being censused: two thirds of a megabyte comes back from grep, and is stored in the fact, per declared target.",
474:   "text": "The maintainer's scope sentence \u2014 no `look` should return tetel's own content \u2014 should not become the printed guarantee, because after this change it is false. `look_path` refuses a directory, reads exactly the file it was handed, and traverses nothing; it can and should still open a snapshot's `prose.jsonl` for a reader who names it, which is how anyone re-checks a prior memo's record against what it claims. The design leaves it entirely alone. The honest guarantee covers both modes in one sentence: a `look` returns tetel's own output only when the caller named it. That is not a weaker promise dressed up \u2014 it is the same rule `look_grep` is being given, since what the exclusions remove is only ever reached by traversal, and it happens to be a rule `look_path` has always satisfied trivially. A reader with only the printed sentence to go on is then told the thing that actually determines whether they will see a snapshot: whether they asked for one.",
478:     "clause": "it happens to be a rule `look_path` has always satisfied trivially",
1226:   "text": "The other `look` path turns out to have a different answer from the one its shape suggests. `look_path` computes `shown` and uses it twice, but not as one value in one place: `printed` is a string of its own that receives a *copy* of `shown` by borrow, and only afterwards is `shown` moved into the pending entry's `output`. Two independent strings exist between those two points, so a bound applied to `printed` there leaves the captured output, the label, the key, the extent, the pin and the snapshot byte-identical \u2014 the same separation `look_grep` has, in a function that reads at first glance as though it has none. There is therefore no code-shaped reason to leave the plain `look <path>` alone, and no other reason either: a whole-file read that overruns the caller's cap is the same silent cut this design exists to stop. So it is bounded too, on the same terms.",
1246:   "text": "Two functions change, both in `observe.rs`. A whole-worktree census of `look_grep` finds five occurrences in two source files \u2014 the definition, one call site in `dispatch`, three doc comments \u2014 and a census of `look_path` finds four in one file: the definition, one call site in the same `dispatch`, two doc comments. No test, no binary and no other module names either of them. The bound, the marker in the returned text and the label segment are all assembled inside each function, and neither signature changes, so nothing calling them has to be touched \u2014 not `dispatch`, not the CLI, not the MCP handler.",
1509:   "text": "Where an asymmetry does survive is inside `look_path`, and it is about what a shortfall means rather than about whether the bound applies. Under `--lines A:B` the author named a range, and the label already records that range as delivered \u2014 clamped to the file's length, or an explicit \"nothing in range\" \u2014 so the shortfall it reports is one the author asked for. A bound biting on top of that is a second shortfall, chosen by tetel rather than by them, and it is recorded beside the first rather than in place of it. Under a plain `look <path>` there is no author-named range at all: the bound is the only shortfall there is, and naming it is the only thing standing between the author and a cut they would never learn about. The spelling is the grep case's, on both surfaces: the label reads `<path> \u2014 showed N of M lines (32768-byte bound)`, or `<path> lines {a}-{end} \u2014 showed N of M lines (32768-byte bound)` where a range was asked for, with M the line count of what was selected before the bound; the returned text ends with the same segment. The release rule is the grep case's too, floor included \u2014 whole lines while a whole line fits, and where none does the first line cut at a character boundary at or below the budget, which the label spells `<path> \u2014 showed 0 of M lines; first line cut mid-line at B of L bytes (32768-byte bound)`. A read that fits gains no segment in either place, and neither case is an error.\n\nThe order of the edit has to be stated for this function specifically, because the instruction given earlier \u2014 bound first, build the label from the bound \u2014 was given about `look_grep`, and `look_grep` is the function whose existing statement order already runs that way. `look_path` runs the other way. Its selection and its label are produced together by one `match` on the requested range, and all three arms of that `match` finish the label before the string the bound applies to has been created at all; the label is then handed to the pending entry untouched. An implementer who bounds the returned string where the selection is pushed into it, and leaves that `match` alone, has written a cut return with a label that says nothing about the cut \u2014 the exact defect this memo exists to remove, on the path it was added to last. So the `match` yields the base label only, and the shortfall segment is appended to it after the release rule has run over the selected text.",

972:    "prop": "\"Transcribed verbatim\" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls \u2014 a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint \u2014 so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection (\"refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact \u2014 the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it\"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.",

23642:        "note": "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."

24032:        "note": "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. That state is reachable here, not hypothetical: F1(7) finds four tracked files in this worktree with a single line over 32768 bytes (up to 905745), and F1(4) confirms `look_path` filters nothing, so any of them can be opened directly. The claim as written establishes only that the cut must fall on a line boundary; it does not establish that a line-boundary cut always returns something, and the design nowhere states what happens when it returns nothing. Either state the floor (admit at least one line, cutting it mid-line and saying so) or state explicitly that a line longer than the budget is unreturnable \u2014 the current wording leaves an implementer to discover the zero-byte case in production."

The clause that does not hold as written is \"`look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory\": `look_path` has a third refusal in its body, `invalid --lines range {a}:{b}` when `a < 1 || a > b` (observe.rs:300-302). 24614:    "prop": "The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.",
24626:        "clause": "in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`",

24666:        "note": "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. So the asymmetry is not \"a consequence of the code's shape\"; it is a choice the design is entitled to make but has not justified. This matters because C9 is an instruction to an implementer \u2014 it tells them the `look <path>` case is closed by construction, which suppresses the observation that after f3 ships, `look <path>` on a large file is still silently cut by the caller with no trace anywhere, the very defect the ticket names."

25615:        "note": "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
25619:        "note": "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
25627:        "note": "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."

26274:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."

26525:        "note": "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
26533:        "note": "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
26537:        "note": "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

596:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
608:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
616:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."

660:    "prop": "The strictness objections to byte-level containment dissolve on the actual capture path, and every weaker relation reopens the invention channel. A donor comment wrapped across lines with interior prefix noise (`//`, `*`, indentation) IS a contiguous byte substring of a look_path capture, because look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim \u2014 the cost is only that the selected premise carries its comment syntax into the rendered section, which the \"never paraphrase\" constraint endorses rather than tolerates. Stripping that noise would require knowing each language's comment syntax, which is precisely the hard-coded per-language coupling scope.rs's \"language-agnostic by construction\" doctrine excludes. Two capture modes genuinely fight containment \u2014 grep-derived match outputs interleave \"lineno:\" prefixes between lines, and whole-search/no-match records carry empty output \u2014 so the design's guidance is that a donor fact is minted from `look` of the donor file; that is guidance about which observation to select from, not a new rule, since the relation is indifferent to which kind produced the bytes. Weaker relations fail: per-line containment lets an author stitch non-adjacent lines into a sentence the donor never wrote, and whitespace- or case-normalised matching means the memo shows text the capture does not contain \u2014 both are paraphrase with extra steps.",
673:        "note": "The capture-path clauses check out with one unstated condition. Grep-derived per-file outputs do carry \"lineno:\" prefixes on every line, and both Search and NoMatch records store empty output \u2014 verified in look_grep. But \"look_path stores the file's bytes verbatim\" is unconditionally true only for the plain open: with --lines, look_path collects contents.lines() and re-joins with \"\\n\", which reproduces the file's bytes for LF files but not for CRLF files (and read_to_string refuses non-UTF-8 entirely). A wrapped donor comment is a contiguous substring of a whole-file capture; for a --lines capture that holds only under the LF condition the proposition does not state."
681:        "note": "Each capture-mode assertion is what observe.rs does: plain look_path stores fs::read_to_string's contents verbatim (no normalisation); --lines stores all[a-1..end].join(\"\\n\"), and Rust's lines() strips \\r on CRLF and the final join drops the trailing newline \u2014 in that mode only, exactly as claimed. So a multi-line prefixed comment is a contiguous substring of the capture in both modes. The two fighting modes are real too: per-file grep entries join \"lineno:\"-prefixed match lines, and the Search/NoMatch whole-search records carry output: String::new(). The stitching argument against per-line containment follows directly from the \"\\n\"-join."
906:        "note": "The \"raw capture\" premise holds: a plain look_path capture stores the donor file's bytes verbatim, so both the single-line clause and the full seven-line comment with its // prefixes are contiguous substrings of such a capture, with no comment-syntax knowledge involved."

1991:    "note": "The code shows `look_path` rejects directories and reads only the supplied file, while `look_grep` adds exclusions only for non-TETEL directory roots. The probes confirm excluded TETEL content is skipped during recursive traversal but remains searchable when the file or TETEL directory is explicitly named.",
1998:        "note": "look_path's half is exact: directory refusal, single fs::read_to_string, no traversal, therefore every file it can return was named by the caller and no exclusion applies to it."
2017:    "prop": "No opt-out flag should be added, because three escape hatches already exist and each is reached by naming something rather than by setting a flag. `look_path` opens any single named file, including one inside a snapshot, and is untouched by this design. `look --grep` rooted at a path that is itself tetel content passes no exclusions at all, which is not merely permitted but forced: grep's `--exclude-dir` suppresses a directory named as the recursion root, so the flags must be withheld there or naming a snapshot directory would return nothing. And `run` spawns `argv` directly with nothing between the empty-argv refusal and the spawn that inspects, parses or classifies the command or the paths it will touch, so it has no place a path exclusion could be applied even in principle. A flag would add a fourth route that, unlike all three of these, leaves no trace in what was named.",
2022:    "note": "The evidence supports the direct `look_path` and `run` behavior and shows that `--exclude-dir` suppresses a snapshot directory used as the recursion root. It does not establish that all exclusions must be withheld (rather than only the root-suppressing one), nor the absolute claim that path exclusion has no possible application in principle.",
2029:        "note": "Escape hatches 1 and 3: look_path opens any single named file with no traversal and nothing in this design touches it; run_command has only the empty-argv refusal between entry and `Command::new(&argv[0]).spawn()`, with no inspection of the command or its paths, so it offers no place to apply an exclusion."
3558:        "note": "True of the bound in isolation; false of the design, and the prose spends the unqualified form. `facts::mint` computes the pin as sha256 over, for every pending entry, `label` + `world_root` + `world_state` + `output` (facts.rs:417-435, its own comment: \"a content fingerprint over every entry's label, output and world-tree marker\"), and copies `label` into the fact's extent (facts.rs:400-411). C17 requires the `Search` label to gain a \"showed N of 883 matching lines (32768-byte bound)\" segment, and C20 requires the same of the `look_path` label. So for any observation on which the bound bites, the extent bytes change, the pin changes, and the snapshot's facts.jsonl changes \u2014 the exact three things this claim says stay byte-identical to today's, and on which the memo rests \"what makes f3 cheap and what keeps it inside the ticket's scope\". F2 shows the crate already reasons this way: the test comment at authoring_cli.rs:508-510 justifies naming memos in the label precisely so that two differently-excluded searches \"would not pin identically\".\n\nThe second half is the implementer-facing bite. This claim's mechanism is that `printed` and the pending entries \"are built separately... neither reads the other\" \u2014 today true, and F1(5) confirms the `Search` label is computed from `root`, `pattern`, `by_file.len()` and `note`, none of which touch `printed`. After the change the label must carry N, a number that exists only as a product of bounding `printed`. The design therefore creates the coupling this claim says is absent, and an implementer who took the claim at face value (\"a bound imposed while assembling `printed` cannot reach the buffer\") would bound `printed` and leave the label alone \u2014 which is the design's own defect back again.\n\nWhat survives unqualified: the captured `output`, the key and the world markers do stay byte-identical, so overlap and re-resolvability are untouched (F1(2),(3): `ExtentEntry::censuses` reads kind/pattern/key/world_root and never the label, and `scope::extent_covers` only enlarges its haystack)."
3631:        "note": "The reason given is sound \u2014 a mid-line cut does hand the author a fragment that is not a match record \u2014 but the rule the design derives from it (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\") has no floor, and with C8's 32768 it admits a return of zero content whenever the first candidate line exceeds the budget. That state is reachable here, not hypothetical: F1(7) finds four tracked files in this worktree with a single line over 32768 bytes (up to 905745), and F1(4) confirms `look_path` filters nothing, so any of them can be opened directly. The claim as written establishes only that the cut must fall on a line boundary; it does not establish that a line-boundary cut always returns something, and the design nowhere states what happens when it returns nothing. Either state the floor (admit at least one line, cutting it mid-line and saying so) or state explicitly that a line longer than the budget is unreturnable \u2014 the current wording leaves an implementer to discover the zero-byte case in production."
3635:        "note": "Everything measurable here checks out: grep is run with -I -n -H so its output line is `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` and `look_grep` splits on `stdout.lines()`; exactly four tracked paths hold a single line over 32768 bytes, up to 905745, and all four are *.tetel/facts.jsonl snapshot ledgers (F3); a whole-`src` grep for `is_char_boundary`, `char_indices` and `.truncate(` returns no hits at all (F3); the longest single line carries 1922 UTF-8 continuation bytes (F6). The clause that does not hold as written is \"`look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory\": `look_path` has a third refusal in its body, `invalid --lines range {a}:{b}` when `a < 1 || a > b` (observe.rs:300-302). The conclusion the clause is used for is unaffected \u2014 no exclusion filtering is applied and a plain `look <path>` with no range reaches none of the three refusals, so each of the four ledgers is readable directly \u2014 but the enumeration is incomplete."
3639:        "note": "The conclusion survives; the inference stated for it does not. C5 argues: the whole-lines-only rule \"admits a return of no content at all whenever the first candidate line by itself exceeds the budget, and that state is reachable on tracked files here rather than hypothetical: exactly four tracked paths in this worktree hold a single line longer than 32768 bytes \u2026 while `look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory and applies no exclusion filtering, so each is readable directly\".\n\nHolding a long line somewhere is not the same as the FIRST candidate line being over budget, and the claim's evidence establishes only the former. Measured (F1): in all four files the long line sits at position 11/15, 15, 2 and 2 \u2014 never position 1 \u2014 with first lines of 978, 882, 1273 and 1237 bytes. Reading each of them \"directly\", i.e. a plain `look <path>`, returns 5, 2, 1 and 1 whole lines (24948, 11977, 1274, 1238 bytes) and never zero content.\n\nThe condition C5 does not state, and needs: the zero-content state arises on a read whose selection BEGINS with the over-budget line \u2014 a ranged `look --lines k:\u2026` with the long line at k (`--lines 15:20` on tet46, `--lines 2:2` on tet29). Under that condition the state is real and the floor is earned. As written, the claim's premise (\"four tracked paths hold a long line\") does not entail its conclusion (\"that state is reachable\" via the direct read it names), and the reader is left believing the plain read is the witness when it is not.\n\nThe rest of C5 \u2014 the line-boundary release rule, the character-boundary snap, the absence of any byte-safe cut in `src/`, the 1922 continuation bytes \u2014 is untouched by this."
3643:        "note": "Every measured component of C5 is exact \u2014 F3 reproduces all of them independently: exactly four tracked paths hold a line over 32768 bytes and all four are tetel's own .tetel/facts.jsonl ledgers, largest line 905745; the over-budget positions are 11 and 15 of 20, 15 of 21, 2 of 11, 2 of 10; a selection from line 1 releases 5, 2, 1 and 1 whole lines and never floors; the longest output line across the nine censuses is 1090 bytes; a whole-src grep for is_char_boundary/char_indices/.truncate( returns no matches; the longest single line carries 1922 UTF-8 continuation bytes. The grep line shape and the split unit are as stated.\n\nThe qualification is one clause: \"`look_path` refuses only a missing path and a directory\". look_path has THREE `workspace::refuse` sites, not two \u2014 the third is `invalid --lines range {a}:{b}` at src/observe.rs:300-302, fired when `a < 1 || a > b`. The \"only\" is false as written. It does not disturb the conclusion drawn from it (each of the four ledgers is readable directly, and the exclusion-filtering half of the clause is correct \u2014 look_path calls no Exclusions::decide and filters nothing), but the third refusal sits inside the very `match lines` block C20 instructs an implementer to restructure, so an implementer told there are only two refusals there is misinformed about the code they are about to edit."
3715:    "prop": "The plain `look <path>` and `look --lines A:B` paths must be left alone by this design, because in `look_path` the returned bytes and the captured `output` are the same value `shown`; bounding the return there would necessarily change what is captured, which the ticket puts out of scope. `look_grep` is bounded and `look_path` is not, and that asymmetry is a consequence of the code's shape, not an oversight.",
3720:    "note": "The code does show that `PendingEntry.output` is `shown`, but `look_path` returns `printed`, which also includes a header and sometimes a trailing newline, so the returned value and captured output are not the same value. The evidence also does not establish that the ticket puts bounding `look_path` out of scope or that the asymmetry is intentional rather than an oversight.",
3727:        "note": "The claim's premise is right and its inference is false. In `look_path` (observe.rs 268-336) `printed` is a separate String assembled by `printed.push_str(&shown)` at line 316 \u2014 a byte copy \u2014 and `shown` is moved into `PendingEntry.output` afterwards at line 325. Two independent Strings exist between those points, which is the same separation `look_grep` exploits. Bounding `printed` after line 316 would therefore NOT \"necessarily change what is captured\": the capture would be byte-identical, exactly as C2 says it is on the grep path. So the asymmetry is not \"a consequence of the code's shape\"; it is a choice the design is entitled to make but has not justified. This matters because C9 is an instruction to an implementer \u2014 it tells them the `look <path>` case is closed by construction, which suppresses the observation that after f3 ships, `look <path>` on a large file is still silently cut by the caller with no trace anywhere, the very defect the ticket names."
3743:    "note": "The `look_path` implementation labels a truncated range as `lines {a}-{end}` with `end = b.min(total)`, and labels an entirely out-of-range request with an explicit \u201cnothing in range\u201d note. This directly establishes the claimed shortfall-recording convention in the module.",
3769:        "note": "Every number checks out on this HEAD: look_grep occurs five times across src/observe.rs and src/worldstate.rs \u2014 definition at observe.rs:349, the single dispatch call at observe.rs:506, doc mentions at observe.rs:76, observe.rs:495 and worldstate.rs:76; look_path four times in src/observe.rs alone \u2014 definition 277, dispatch call 516, doc mentions 4 and 495. No test file, no binary and no other module names either. One point of care rather than a qualification: a raw whole-worktree grep also matches rendered memos, `.evidence.jsonl` files and `.tetel/` ledgers, which is exactly the tetel-output class a census withholds, so \"five times in two files\" is the census's count, not the raw grep's."
3857:        "note": "This claim instructs an implementer what a declared modification target (`NON_COVERAGE`) must say, and what it specifies is census-shaped while the design is not. Its content sentence is \"a fact's extent records the whole search, and nothing anywhere establishes that the author read all of it\", and the prose spends it the same way (\"the list carries the general statement that a census's return to its author is bounded\"), as does C16 (\"the static list says a census reports the tree minus what tetel withheld\"). But C9 and C20 put `look_path` inside the same bound, and F1(4) confirms a plain `look <path>` is a wholly different act \u2014 no search, no root, no exclusions, an extent naming one file and a range. An implementer who writes the line this claim specifies leaves every bounded path read with no standing statement anywhere in `check`'s non-coverage list, which is the one surface the design nominates for the general case. The single-line decision may well still be right, but the line has to be written for both acts \u2014 \"what `look` returns to its author is bounded, and nothing establishes the author read the whole of what the extent records\" \u2014 not for a census. As it stands the claim's own wording, followed literally, produces a line that covers `look_grep` only."
3861:        "note": "report.rs:86-190 carries both entries and the comment between them verbatim: the platform-accident entry (\"symlinked directories and binary files\"), the tetel-output entry, and \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\". No entry in the list concerns what `look` returned to its author. `look_path` applying no exclusion filtering is F2 and is also stated in the tetel-output entry itself; scope.rs naming interpretation/insincere examination as permanently out of reach is F5."
3869:        "note": "The verifiable parts hold. The standing list does discriminate a chosen withholding from platform accidents, and its comment says verbatim \"A deliberate exclusion earns its own line, by the same standard as every other entry here\", beside the entry naming grep skipping symlinked directories and binary files. The first half's factual load is correct: `run_command` returns the child's whole captured output unmeasured with no length test anywhere in the function, and both front ends hand it back whole (`print!(\"{}\", outcome.printed)` in main.rs's Run arm; `\"output\": outcome.printed` in the MCP run tool); the run tool's own description does contemplate \"a command whose output is enormous\" and answers by warning rather than bounding. `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering at all.\n\nThe qualification is the clause \"`scope.rs` names that second half as permanently out of reach\". The only occurrence of \"permanently out of reach\" in the whole of src/ is src/scope.rs:42, and what it registers there is a different proposition: \"Whether the note is *correct* about the location it names is exactly the limit this project registered as permanently out of reach (\\\"insincere examination\\\" \u2014 capture makes the extent honest, not the interpretation).\" That is about the truth of an author's interpretation of a location, not about how much of a capture the author was shown. Reading it as naming the second half (\"a fact's extent records the whole of what was observed, and nothing establishes that the author was shown all of it\") requires stretching \"insincere examination\" from not-examined to not-shown, and scope.rs does not spell that out. This matters because it is the clause carrying the memo's assurance that the new entry \"names an old limit that had been invisible rather than admitting a new weakness\" \u2014 after the bound, `look` genuinely shows the author less than the extent records, which is new. Separate, non-blocking: the list itself is `NON_COVERAGE` in src/report.rs:86, not in scope.rs; C15 does not misattribute it, but the two files are easy to conflate here."
3915:        "note": "The numbers and the unit are confirmed independently (F6): reproducing look_grep's own exclusion set and running the grep gives exactly 883 matching lines and 70 distinct first-colon fields, and appending one trailing parenthesised exclusion-note line raises the distinct-field count to 71, which is the stated cause of the earlier figure. `by_file.len()` is indeed the count of distinct first-colon fields and is computed from the full stdout (F2), and `stdout.lines()` is what look_grep splits on. The clause that does not hold as written is the closing analogy, \"which is how `look --lines` already annotates a range only when it was clamped\": look_path writes `{path} lines {a}-{end}` into the label on every ranged read, clamped or not (observe.rs:308-309), so the range annotation is not clamp-conditional. What is conditional is only the empty-selection form `{path} lines {a}-{b} (file has {total} line(s); nothing in range)`. The analogy therefore overstates the existing convention; the proposed \"absence means whole\" behaviour for the shortfall segment is not itself in question."
3938:        "note": "The `look_path` half of this claim \u2014 \"`--lines A:B` is already a first-class parameter of the same verb, so the author reads the rest of the file by asking for it\" \u2014 is broken by a state reachable on tracked files in this worktree.\n\nConstruction. Take `look /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel/docs/design/tet46-look-never-returns-tetel-content.md.tetel/facts.jsonl`. F1(7) measures it: 20 lines, of which two exceed 32768 bytes, the longest 905745. F1(4) confirms `look_path` applies no exclusion filtering of any kind, so a named snapshot path is read like any other file \u2014 nothing stops this call. Under the rule the design states (\"accumulate whole lines, and stop before the first line that would carry the total past the byte budget\", C5/C20), the return stops at whichever over-budget line comes first. The author then asks for the rest with `--lines k:20`. The selection now BEGINS with a 905745-byte line, no whole line fits under 32768, and the bound admits zero lines: the author gets the `==> path <==` header, an empty body, and a label reading \"showed 0 of N lines (32768-byte bound)\". Every range that includes that line behaves identically. There is no `--lines` argument that returns any byte of it, so the claim's remedy does not reach it, and \"needs nothing new either\" is false: this case needs something the design does not have (a floor of one line, a byte-level fallback for an over-budget line, or at minimum an explicit statement that an over-budget line is unreadable through `look`).\n\nWorse than the status quo on exactly the axis the ticket cares about. Today the caller truncates at ~59 KB, so the author reading that file sees its first ~59 KB. Under the design they see zero bytes of that line. The memo's answer to \"what does an author do\" is that the design \"does not give the author back what was withheld; it stops the withholding from being secret\" \u2014 but here the design withholds strictly more than the status quo did, and this claim asserts a remedy that does not exist.\n\nThe same construction reaches `look_grep`: a grep whose matching line is one of these long JSON lines emits a `<file>:<lineno>:<text>` line over the budget, and if it is the first matching line the bounded return is empty while the label still says \"N files matched\". The prose's consolation that \"even a heavily bounded return still tells the author truthfully how many files matched\" is then a file count attached to nothing."
3973:        "note": "The exemption holds for the grep label and does not extend to the `look_path` label the revision brought inside the bound. Every reason this claim gives is grep-shaped: \"the `Search` entry's `output` is empty and the per-file entries record what was captured, not how much of it was returned\". For `look_path` neither is true. F1(4): the `Path` entry's `output` is `shown` \u2014 the complete selected text, in original order, moved in whole \u2014 and F1(6): facts.jsonl, carrying that output, ships into the snapshot. So for the `look_path` label required by C20, N is a pure function of shipped data and a documented constant: replay whole lines of the stored `output` until 32768 is passed and you have N. That is exactly the class the doctrine (F15/lib.rs:136-141) says to recompute rather than persist, and this claim's stated ground for the exemption \u2014 \"unrecoverable from the ledger after the fact\" \u2014 is false there. The conclusion may still be defensible for `look_path` on other grounds (an author-facing label is not a stored derivation to be recomputed by `check`), but the memo does not make that argument, and this claim's argument does not cover half of what the design writes the number into. Grep is untouched by this: the `Search` output is empty and `by_file` is a BTreeMap, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not recoverable from the per-file entries."
3981:        "note": "The conclusion holds; the two-paths distinction the claim draws does not, on the mode axis. C19 says that for `look_grep` the number is \"plainly outside the rule\" because the per-file entries \"are keyed into a `BTreeMap` by filename, so the stdout order the bound consumed is not in the ledger and N is unrecoverable from it\", and reserves the two fallback grounds for `look_path`. `look_grep` is two instruments selected by one argument value: `-r` is pushed only `if root_path.is_dir()` (observe.rs:352-353) and `Exclusions::decide` returns `None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for a non-directory root, so `look --grep <pattern> <one file>` is a first-class mode, exercised at tests/authoring_cli.rs:473 and :485. In that mode `by_file` has exactly one key and its `Vec<String>` holds every matched line's `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order \u2014 the order the bound consumed \u2014 and the shipped `GrepMatch` entry carries that Vec joined by \"\\n\" as its `output` with `{file} (grep: {pattern})` as its label, so the `{file}:` prefix the bound counted is recoverable too. Full stdout is reconstructible byte-for-byte, and the design's own label states the budget it applied, so replaying the release rule reproduces N exactly. What C19 asserts is unrecoverable is recoverable in this mode. The claim's conclusion survives untouched, because the two grounds it states for `look_path` \u2014 that a replay answers what today's build would show rather than what this author was shown, and that a label's audience holds a rendered memo with no captured output in front of them \u2014 apply verbatim to a single-file grep. The narrowing owed is that the ledger-order argument covers only the recursive mode, and that both paths rest on the same two grounds wherever it does not."
3985:        "note": "Read directly in src/observe.rs. Recursive mode: the Search entry's `output` is `String::new()`, and the per-file entries are collected into `by_file: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` keyed by filename, so grep's stdout order \u2014 the order a bound would consume \u2014 is not in the ledger. Two instruments by one argument value: `args.push(\"-r\")` runs only inside `if root_path.is_dir()`, and `Exclusions::decide` (observe.rs:240-259) returns `Exclusions::None { why: \"the caller named one file\" }` for any non-directory root, verbatim. In single-file mode `-H` is pushed unconditionally so every line is `{file}:{lineno}:{text}` and `split_once(':')` yields one constant key, hence exactly one by_file entry whose Vec holds every matched line as `{lineno}:{text}` in stdout order, shipped as `output: matches.join(\"\\n\")` under `label: format!(\"{file} (grep: {pattern})\")` \u2014 file, order and every matched line all in the ledger, so the full stdout reconstructs from that one entry. For look_path, `PendingEntry { output: shown, .. }` receives the complete selection."

157:      <p class="prop">"Transcribed verbatim" cannot be an honour-system field, and does not need to be: <mark>the decidable relation is that a premise's text is refused unless it is a verbatim substring of the cited donor fact's captured output</mark>. Both sides of that comparison are Strings the tool controls — a fact's output is produced only by look/run (file bytes read verbatim by look_path, grep match lines, a process's merged stream), no authoring surface lets anyone supply output by hand, and output is immutable after mint — so substring containment is a pure byte-level comparison with no normalisation step owned by the check. Typing is the selection mechanism, not the trust: the author types the premise, but a typed premise the donor never wrote fails containment and is refused at the verb. This is exactly the README's Direction item for supporting-span selection ("refused unless it is a verbatim substring of a cited fact — the author cannot type an extent, and here could not invent support, only select it"), and TET-29 is the first place it becomes load-bearing rather than roadmap.</p>

note: Re-derived independently on 2026-08-22 in a fresh scratch tree: the untraversed spelling of the working directory DOES exist in a process, contrary to the memo's impossibility clause. Fixture: `outer` and `otherrepo` are two real git repositories side by side; `outer/link` is a committed symlink to `../otherrepo`. After a shell `cd $S/outer/link`, an external child process (/usr/bin/python3) inherits PWD=$S/outer/link — the untraversed spelling — while getcwd() reports $S/otherrepo, and os.path.realpath(PWD)==os.getcwd() is True. Control: after `cd $S/outer`, PWD==getcwd()==$S/outer and the validity test is also True. Degraded arms, both of which the memo already states correctly and which survive: with the chdir performed by the process itself rather than by a shell, PWD stayed at the shell's directory ($S/outer), getcwd() was $S/otherrepo, and realpath(PWD)==getcwd() is False — so a validity test discards it; and under `env -i` PWD is absent entirely (None) while getcwd() still answers. Consequence: a guard reading PWD, trusting it only when realpath(PWD)==getcwd() and otherwise falling back to getcwd, refuses the escaping capture (PWD $S/outer/link does not lie under the answering root $S/otherrepo) and accepts the control unchanged (PWD $S/outer lies under $S/outer). The guard is therefore partial, not unavailable.

/// A caller-supplied path, resolved to absolute for every message that
/// names it.
///
/// The server cannot know the caller's working directory, so a relative
/// path silently means something different to each side. Nothing here
/// changes *which* file is opened — that was always resolved against this
/// process's directory — but it makes the resolution visible in the
/// answer, so "no tetel rows found in /somewhere/unexpected/memo.md"
/// diagnoses itself instead of reading as a fact about the document.
fn resolved(path: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    let p = Path::new(path);
    if p.is_absolute() {
        return p.to_path_buf();
    }
    std::env::current_dir().map(|d| d.join(p)).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_path_buf())
}
